name: Evaluations
summary: azure-ai-evaluation >=1.18.2: judge LLM via a `{byo_model, project_endpoint}` model_config.
description: Prompty-based judge evaluators (`RelevanceEvaluator`, `CoherenceEvaluator`, `FluencyEvaluator`, etc.) accept a `model_config` dict shaped as `{"byo_model": "{connection}/{deployment}", "project_endpoint": "..."}`. When both keys are present, `azure-ai-evaluation` routes the judge call through the Foundry project Responses API (`_byo_judge.AsyncByoProjectResponsesClient`) instead of building a native `/openai/deployments/{deployment}/...` URL, so the AI Gateway connection is resolved server-side.
notes:
Fixed in `azure-ai-evaluation` 1.18.2 (2026-07-21 changelog: "Added support for admin-connected (BYO) judge models in prompty-based evaluators"). Verified live against a public (non-PE) Foundry + APIM AI Gateway pair with `azure-ai-evaluation==1.18.5`:

```python
model_config = {"byo_model": f"{apim_conn}/gpt-5-mini", "project_endpoint": project_endpoint}
RelevanceEvaluator(model_config=model_config)(query="What is 2+2?", response="4")
# -> {'relevance_result': 'pass', 'relevance_score': 4.0, ...}
```

The *old* `AzureOpenAIModelConfiguration(azure_deployment="{conn}/{model}")` shape is still broken on the same environment -- it builds `/openai/deployments/{conn}/{model}/chat/completions`, which Foundry rejects with `400 'API version not supported'`. `_BYOModelConfiguration` is not yet exported as a public type (SDK docstring: "not caller-facing... until the feature reaches GA"), so pass a plain dict with the two required keys, not the typed config classes.

Not yet verified: cloud-submitted evaluation jobs (`project.evaluations.create(...)` with `initialization_parameters.deployment_name`) -- this probe only covers the local synchronous evaluator path. Requires `azure-ai-evaluation>=1.18.2`; set `EVAL_JUDGE_MODEL` to run.
